answer.rationale: On day 71, the incumbent refuses to reopen pricing, the mandate demands an 18% cost cut, and the low-cost vendor's standalone quote meets the mandate. memory_c2 was the basis for trusting the low-cost vendor: quick onboarding and accurate invoicing under prior onboarding. Before committing a full switch while the line runs at 94% of committed volume, I will verify c2's original record once (max budget) to confirm whether that confidence was built under similar scale, terms, and quality constraints. The intended action is to switch primary vendor for the constrained component, but I will stage it as a small, guarded test — a bounded first run with a fallback to the incumbent if quality, lead time, or volume commitments slip — so that delivery risk does not rise. add_second_source and defer_decision are not selected because (a) adding a second source does not on its own satisfy the cost-cut mandate against an incumbent that refuses to move, and (b) deferring loses the 14-day window with no auto-renew, forcing a higher-risk decision later. negotiate_terms is foreclosed by the incumbent's stated refusal. Renegotiation for the long term (memory_c4 / memory_c6) is not available this cycle; it can be pursued with the new vendor after the contract is awarded.
